The one big ISRO story this week: on Thu 12 Nov, ISRO successfully ground-tested the redesigned third stage (PS3) of its PSLV rocket at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

Why it matters: The third stage showed problems in the last two PSLV missions, C61 (EOS-09) and C62 (EOS-N1). ISRO then reviewed the whole stage: design margins, raw material checks, assembly and quality tests.
What changed: The nozzle design is stronger, the joints have backup sealing, and the material, assembly and non-destructive testing steps are updated.
What it was not: This was a test on the ground, not a launch. ISRO says more tests are planned after it studies the data.

This comes from one report (Amar Ujala, quoting ISRO's statement via ANI), and I only saw part of the page. I found nothing else for Thu 5 Nov to Thu 12 Nov, so other ISRO news from that week may be missing.
